1	# Harness Skills Changelog
     2	
     3	This file records coordinated changes to the harness skills suite. It is not a release manifest or
     4	installation record. Feature-local `changelog.md` files remain the append-only history for one
     5	Feature and must not be used as suite maintenance notes.
     6	
     7	## Unreleased
     8	
     9	No unreleased suite changes are recorded.
    10	
    11	## 2026-07-23 - Idea Intake And Contract Lifecycle
    12	
    13	### Added
    14	
    15	- Added the explicit, docs-only `add-idea` entry point.
    16	- Added one-question-at-a-time Grill behavior with a user-confirmed shared-understanding gate.
    17	- Added independent owner routes: `CREATE_FEATURE`, `PATCH_FEATURE`, and `BLOCKED_OWNER`.
    18	- Added independent artifact routes for requirements, Specs, ADR candidates, state-only changes, and
    19	  `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE`.
    20	- Added a shared Feature/Requirements/Spec/ADR ownership and lifecycle contract.
    21	- Added Spec, Spec index, ADR, and decision index templates.
    22	- Added routing eval cases for vague ideas, new Features, existing Feature patches, blocking ADRs,
    23	  and reversible local changes.
    24	- Added [`UPGRADING.md`](UPGRADING.md) for manual, per-project maintenance of existing skill copies.
    25	
    26	### Changed
    27	
    28	- Separated long-lived Feature lifecycle from bounded Spec implementation and validation lifecycle.
    29	- Reduced Feature README ownership to current state, route, blockers, next gate, and contract links.
    30	- Kept expected behavior, acceptance, NFRs, non-goals, and stop rules in `requirements.md`.
    31	- Moved bounded implementation interfaces, schema, state, module boundaries, migration, testing, and
    32	  validation matrices into Specs.
    33	- Required confirmed requirements, accepted blocking ADRs, and a frozen Spec before later
    34	  contract-affecting implementation can become implementation-ready.
    35	- Updated project analysis, project docs, external collaboration, bootstrap, demo, and runtime gate
    36	  guidance to use the new contract.
    37	- Defined trigger-based migration for existing Feature documents instead of bulk rewriting them.
    38	
    39	### Removed
    40	
    41	- Removed the curated bundle manifest and automated bundle installer.
    42	- Removed bundle versions, installation markers, automatic overwrite, and suite-level deployment
    43	  semantics. Harness skills are maintained individually in each target project.
    44	
    45	### Maintenance Notes
    46	
    47	- Existing Feature documents remain valid legacy inputs and migrate only when related work touches
    48	  them.
    49	- Target-owned `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules`, `docs/OVERVIEW.md`, Feature documents, and
    50	  project code must be changed only through the target project's normal reviewed workflow.
    51	- Existing projects may maintain all harness skills, a subset, or project-specific extensions. Do
    52	  not add missing skills unless the target project needs and accepts them.
    53	- Follow [`UPGRADING.md`](UPGRADING.md) to audit layout, compare individual skills, preserve local
    54	  changes, validate target-specific routes, and roll back through version control.
    55	
    56	## Earlier History
    57	
    58	Earlier harness copies had no suite-level changelog. They may use grouped, flat, partial, or
    59	project-customized skill layouts. Treat their current files and target repository history as the
    60	migration evidence; do not infer a common installed version.
     1	# Maintaining And Upgrading Harness Skills
     2	
     3	This repository maintains canonical harness skills and shared documentation contracts. It does not
     4	provide a bundle installer, manifest, installation marker, automatic overwrite, or fleet deployment
     5	tool. Every target project chooses which skills it maintains and upgrades them through its own
     6	reviewed change process.
     7	
     8	## Ownership Boundary
     9	
    10	| Surface | Owner | Maintenance rule |
    11	|---|---|---|
    12	| Canonical `skills/harness/<skill>/` | This source repository | Defines the current reusable skill |
    13	| Target project skill copy | Target project | Compare and update individually |
    14	| Root/nested `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` | Target project | Patch existing sections; never replace wholesale |
    15	| `.cursor/rules` and other runtime rules | Target project | Keep consistent with accepted target policy |
    16	| `docs/OVERVIEW.md`, indexes, Features, Specs, ADRs, changelogs | Target project | Migrate only through project-owned docs workflows |
    17	| Source code, tests, configuration, artifacts, and evidence | Target project | Never changed merely because a skill changed |
    18	
    19	A canonical skill update is a maintenance input, not authorization to change a target project. A
    20	proposal, shared-understanding confirmation, existing implementation, or copied skill also does not
    21	grant implementation, deployment, publication, training, or destructive-operation authorization.
    22	
    23	## Supported Target Layouts

    43	```

   118	  contract-affecting implementation;

   120	- keep always-on runtime rules consistent with root instructions.

   123	updated in place.

   126

   128

   131	3. Create a new Spec only for a bounded implementation contract; do not overwrite validated or
   132	   superseded historical Specs.
   133	4. Create an ADR only when the decision is costly to reverse, would be confusing without context,
   134	   and has real alternatives with material trade-offs.
   135	5. Keep README focused on current state, active routes, blockers, next gate, and links.
   136	6. Append durable route and lifecycle transitions to the Feature changelog.
   137	7. Use `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE` for reversible local details that change no durable truth.
   138	
   139	An untouched legacy Feature can remain in its old shape. Before its next contract-affecting
   140	implementation, establish confirmed requirements, resolve blocking ADRs, and freeze the active Spec.
   141	
   142	## Validation
   143	
   144	After maintaining each target project:
   145	
   146	- review `git diff` and confirm unrelated changes remain untouched;

   153	- run `git diff --check`.

   156	diff and validation evidence are the completion criteria.
   157	
   158	## Rollback
   159

   161	Rollback uses that target project's normal version-control process. Restore the previous individual
   162	skill files and governance sections together; do not leave new producer contracts with old consumer
   163	skills, or new registry entries pointing to removed paths.
   164	
   165	Preserve failed migration evidence until the target owner confirms restoration. Rollback does not
   166	imply that active Feature or code changes made under separate authorization should also be reverted.
   167	
   168	## Multi-Project Rollout
   169	
   170	Maintain multiple projects in small, reviewable groups:
   171	
   172	1. Inventory each target's grouped, flat, partial, or extended layout.
   173	2. Record which coordinated skills each target actually uses.
   174	3. Compare files read-only and classify local differences.

   178	7. Migrate Feature documents only when active work touches them.

   183	reviewed diff, and validation evidence are the source of truth for its maintained skill state.

    10	
    11	# Document Organization Harness
    12	
    13	Use this skill when a repo needs a portable harness layer: a root instruction
    14	file, a navigable docs map, explicit module ownership, and a documentation tree
    15	an agent can follow without guessing the repo shape.
    16	
    17	## Outcome
    18	
    19	Deliver the smallest useful harness that still gives an agent clear entry points:
    20	
    21	- root `AGENTS.md` or equivalent
    22	- optional `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` for an always-applied contract,
    23	  validation, and documentation synchronization gate
    24	- `docs/OVERVIEW.md`
    25	- `docs/feature/INDEX.md`
    26	- `docs/reference/INDEX.md`
    27	- `docs/collaboration/INDEX.md`
    28	- `docs/archive/INDEX.md`
    29	- module-level `README.md` / `INDEX.md` plus `requirements.md` for expected
    30	  product or business behavior and acceptance
    31	- lazy `specs/` for bounded implementation contracts and `decisions/` for ADRs
    32	- owning GOAL/README sections for completed work, pending work, blockers, and
    33	  the next validation gate
    34	- leaf docs with explicit parent links
    35	
    36	## Workflow
    37	
    38	1. Inspect existing root instructions, docs, and ownership boundaries.
    39	2. Identify the repo's real layers before writing any new structure.
    40	3. Create or repair the docs map first; distinguish `requirements.md` for
    41	   expected behavior, Specs for bounded implementation contracts, ADRs for
    42	   durable rationale, and `README.md` / `INDEX.md` for current state/routing.
    43	4. Route durable progress through the owning GOAL/README instead of creating a
    44	   separate execution-control document.
    45	5. Write leaf docs only after the parent indexes exist.
    46	6. Record stable validation evidence in owning docs or append-only artifacts.
    47	7. Keep top-down discoverability and bottom-up traceability intact.
    48	8. Validate that an agent can start at `AGENTS.md`, find the next doc, and walk
    49	   back.
    50	
    51	## Rules
    52	
    53	- Treat docs as routing, not as a dumping ground.
    54	- Keep business content out of the harness layer.
    55	- Keep stack-specific details in repo-local adapters or references.
    56	- Prefer repairing an existing partial harness over replacing it.
    57	- Use root-relative links for deep cross-tree references.
    58	- Keep expected behavior, current implementation, current progress, and
    59	  historical evidence distinct, with each routed to its owning durable file.
    60	- Do not persist transient decomposition solely to coordinate the current
    61	  session; use the session's planning surface instead.
    62	- Before non-trivial implementation, freeze module owners, public interfaces,
    63	  dependency direction, mutable-state ownership, file budgets, and test ownership.
    64	- Keep new or changed handwritten files at or below 1000 physical lines; at
    65	  800 lines, review responsibility-based extraction with `refactor-large-modules`.
    66	- Delegation is never implied by this skill. When a user explicitly requests
    67	  delegation, use bounded owner scopes and isolated worktrees where needed.
    68	- **Enforcement must be runtime-injected, not just described.** In a Cursor
    69	  repo, keep the contract, validation, evidence, and documentation synchronization
    70	  gate in BOTH `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`) and
    71	  root `AGENTS.md`.
    72	
    73	## Reference
    74	
    75	Read `references/harness-bootstrap.md` for:
    76	
    77	- AGENTS.md section order
    78	- docs tree templates
    79	- sample feature module with README + requirements separation
    80	- owning GOAL/README status rules
    81	- leaf-document link rules
    82	- validation checklist
    83	- per-project skill maintenance and contract migration
    84	
    85	## Demo Pack
    86	
    87	If the target repo needs a fast bootstrap, adapt the included demo harness from
    88	`assets/demo-harness/` and replace every placeholder with target-project facts.
    89	The demo pack includes:
    90	
    91	- a root `AGENTS.md` with documentation governance and execution-safety rules
    92	- a Cursor-native `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` gate (`alwaysApply: true`)
    93	- the `docs/` entry points
    94	- reference docs for architecture, interfaces, and validation
    95	- one sample feature module showing README + requirements separation
    96	
    97	Use it as a starting shape, not as a final domain model.
    98	
    99	## Suite Maintenance Boundary
   100	
   101	This repository is the canonical maintenance source for independent harness skills. It does not
   102	provide a bundle manifest, installer, automatic overwrite, or target-project upgrade command.
   103	Projects may maintain the full suite, a subset, or local extensions in grouped or flat paths.
   104	
   105	`add-idea` is the explicit docs-only intake for unclear or clear product/engineering ideas. It runs
   106	the Grill protocol when needed, chooses a new or existing Feature owner, and materializes
   107	requirements, Specs, and conditional ADRs before later implementation workflows.
   108	
   109	Recommended maintenance flow:
   110	
   111	1. Read the suite [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) and
   112	   [`UPGRADING.md`](../UPGRADING.md).
   113	2. Inspect the target project's actual skill registry, layout, local extensions, and working tree.
   114	3. Compare and update only the individual skills the target uses; do not normalize paths or replace
   115	   directories containing unclassified local content.
   116	4. When adopting the full lifecycle change, maintain shared contracts first, then producer and
   117	   consumer skills, then patch target-owned governance.
   118	5. Follow the suite [`AGENTS.md` patch contract](../README.md) to incrementally update existing target
   119	   rules; never replace target-owned rules or Feature docs.
   120	
   121	See `references/harness-bootstrap.md` for docs scaffolding and maintenance order. Target repository
   122	history, reviewed diffs, and validation evidence remain the truth for what that project maintains.

    29	| Skills | 仅注册实际安装的 harness skills |
    30	| Delegation / Worktrees | 明确“用户授权后才允许” |
    31	| Testing | 保留项目原命令，补充从聚焦到广泛的验证顺序 |
    32	
    33	## 无等价章节时追加的 Managed Block
    34	
    35	把下方内容追加到根 `AGENTS.md`，并把不适用于目标仓库的条件项删掉。不得保留占位符或无效路径。
    36	
    37	```md
    38	<!-- HARNESS-GOVERNANCE:START -->
    39	## Harness 文档与实施门禁
    40	
    41	### 上下文与渐进式披露
    42	
    43	- 项目上下文入口：[`docs/OVERVIEW.md`](docs/OVERVIEW.md)。
    44	- 按 `AGENTS.md -> docs/OVERVIEW.md -> feature/reference/collaboration/archive INDEX -> 1-3 个任务相关 leaf` 逐层读取；禁止全量读取 `docs/`。
    45	- 新 idea 统一从 `.agents/skills/harness/add-idea` 进入：边界不清时逐题 Grill，确认后由 Agent 选择新建 Feature 或 patch 现有 Feature，并按需生成 requirements、Spec 与 ADR。
    46	- `requirements.md` 持有 expected behavior 与 acceptance；active frozen Spec 持有 bounded implementation contract；accepted ADR 持有 durable architecture rationale；当前代码持有 implemented behavior；不可变 artifact、ledger 和 gate report 持有 evidence。
    47	- owning README/GOAL 持有 current state、completed、pending、blockers 和 next validation gate；会话计划只持有本轮临时顺序。
    48	- 外部 proposal 只提供 provenance/recommendation，先完成内部采纳与合同转译，不能直接作为实现合同或授权。
    49	
    50	### Mandatory Execution Gate
    51	
    52	非 trivial 实施前按顺序完成：
    53	
    54	1. 未成形 idea 先进入 `add-idea`；随后定位 owning module、requirements、active Spec、accepted ADR、README/GOAL、稳定 reference 和当前代码入口。
    55	2. contract-affecting implementation 必须引用 frozen Spec；冻结安全与授权边界、schema、公共接口、依赖方向、可变状态 owner、文件预算、测试归属和 validation matrix。
    56	3. 把 durable completed/pending/blockers/next gate 写回唯一 owning README/GOAL；临时执行顺序只放会话计划。
    57	4. 确认当前动作直接推进 active goal，且没有从开发状态、代码存在或实验结果推导出额外执行授权。
    58	5. 在声明边界内实施，保留无关修改；先跑聚焦验证，再跑影响范围支持的广泛检查。
    59	6. 验证通过后同步 owning docs、索引、changelog 和声明的 append-only evidence；没有实质影响时不要制造形式化文档改动。
    60	
    61	禁止把 `taskBoard`、`.agents/tasks` 或其他平行进度文件作为活跃控制面。禁止在用户未明确要求时委派 SubAgent 或强制并行开发。
    62	
    63	### Code Organization Gate
    64	
    65	- CLI、adapter、strategy、model 和 runner 保持薄入口；domain、state、I/O、reporting 和 orchestration 各有明确 owner。
    66	- 新增或本轮修改的手写代码文件不得超过 1000 物理行；达到 800 行时必须进行职责拆分评审。
    67	- 按稳定责任与公共接口拆分，不创建 numbered `part` 文件，也不建立无边界 `utils/common/helpers`。
    68	- 触发拆分时使用 `.agents/skills/harness/refactor-large-modules`，先冻结公共契约和行为基线，再按叶子优先迁移并验证等价性。
    69	
    70	### Repo-local Harness Skills
    71	
    72	- `.agents/skills/harness/add-idea`：统一接收 idea；必要时逐题 Grill，然后路由到新 Feature 或已有 Feature，并创建/patch requirements、Spec 与 conditional ADR，不实施代码。
    73	- `.agents/skills/harness/document-organization-harness`：建立或修复 AGENTS、docs 路由、所有权和治理规则。
    74	- `.agents/skills/harness/progressive-disclosure-docs`：审计渐进式披露、真值所有权、Feature 生命周期和主线路由。
    75	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-analysis`：在 shallow docs 不足时分析架构、数据流、路线影响和 expected-vs-implemented gap。
    76	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-docs-workflow`：编排非 trivial 开发前后的 owning docs、路线、状态和证据写回。
    77	- `.agents/skills/harness/external-collaboration-workflow`：管理外部问题包、方案 provenance、逐项采纳和内部合同转译。
    78	- `.agents/skills/harness/refactor-large-modules`：在保持行为与公共契约的前提下拆分大文件或混合职责模块。
    79	<!-- HARNESS-GOVERNANCE:END -->
    80	```
    81	
    82	## Patch 后验证
    83	
    84	Agent 在结束前必须确认：
    85	
    86	- `git diff -- AGENTS.md` 只包含预期的增量合并，原有安全、授权、所有权和测试规则未丢失；
    87	- managed block 最多一个，已有等价章节没有被重复创建；
    88	- `docs/OVERVIEW.md`、各 INDEX 和注册的 skill 路径真实存在，链接可从上到下到达并能反向返回；
    89	- `AGENTS.md` 不把 taskboard、SubAgent、并行派发、worktree、训练或执行权限设为默认要求；
    90	- 详细流程仍留在 skill/reference 中，根 `AGENTS.md` 只保留稳定规则、路由和硬门禁；
    91	- 若目标仓库使用 `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc`，其 contract、validation、docs write-back
    92	  和 delegation boundary 与 `AGENTS.md` 一致；
    93	- 使用目标仓库已有的 docs、链接、lint 和测试验证命令；不要凭空发明项目命令。
    94	
    95	## 相关入口

    10	
    11	# Document Organization Harness
    12	
    13	Use this skill when a repo needs a portable harness layer: a root instruction
    14	file, a navigable docs map, explicit module ownership, and a documentation tree
    15	an agent can follow without guessing the repo shape.
    16	
    17	## Outcome
    18	
    19	Deliver the smallest useful harness that still gives an agent clear entry points:
    20	
    21	- root `AGENTS.md` or equivalent
    22	- optional `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` for an always-applied contract,
    23	  validation, and documentation synchronization gate
    24	- `docs/OVERVIEW.md`
    25	- `docs/feature/INDEX.md`
    26	- `docs/reference/INDEX.md`
    27	- `docs/collaboration/INDEX.md`
    28	- `docs/archive/INDEX.md`
    29	- module-level `README.md` / `INDEX.md` plus `requirements.md` for expected
    30	  product or business behavior and acceptance
    31	- lazy `specs/` for bounded implementation contracts and `decisions/` for ADRs
    32	- owning GOAL/README sections for completed work, pending work, blockers, and
    33	  the next validation gate
    34	- leaf docs with explicit parent links
    35	
    36	## Workflow
    37	
    38	1. Inspect existing root instructions, docs, and ownership boundaries.
    39	2. Identify the repo's real layers before writing any new structure.
    40	3. Create or repair the docs map first; distinguish `requirements.md` for
    41	   expected behavior, Specs for bounded implementation contracts, ADRs for
    42	   durable rationale, and `README.md` / `INDEX.md` for current state/routing.
    43	4. Route durable progress through the owning GOAL/README instead of creating a
    44	   separate execution-control document.
    45	5. Write leaf docs only after the parent indexes exist.
    46	6. Record stable validation evidence in owning docs or append-only artifacts.
    47	7. Keep top-down discoverability and bottom-up traceability intact.
    48	8. Validate that an agent can start at `AGENTS.md`, find the next doc, and walk
    49	   back.
    50	
    51	## Rules
    52	
    53	- Treat docs as routing, not as a dumping ground.
    54	- Keep business content out of the harness layer.
    55	- Keep stack-specific details in repo-local adapters or references.
    56	- Prefer repairing an existing partial harness over replacing it.
    57	- Use root-relative links for deep cross-tree references.
    58	- Keep expected behavior, current implementation, current progress, and
    59	  historical evidence distinct, with each routed to its owning durable file.
    60	- Do not persist transient decomposition solely to coordinate the current
    61	  session; use the session's planning surface instead.
    62	- Before non-trivial implementation, freeze module owners, public interfaces,
    63	  dependency direction, mutable-state ownership, file budgets, and test ownership.
    64	- Keep new or changed handwritten files at or below 1000 physical lines; at
    65	  800 lines, review responsibility-based extraction with `refactor-large-modules`.
    66	- Delegation is never implied by this skill. When a user explicitly requests
    67	  delegation, use bounded owner scopes and isolated worktrees where needed.
    68	- **Enforcement must be runtime-injected, not just described.** In a Cursor
    69	  repo, keep the contract, validation, evidence, and documentation synchronization
    70	  gate in BOTH `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`) and
    71	  root `AGENTS.md`.
    72	
    73	## Reference
    74	
    75	Read `references/harness-bootstrap.md` for:
    76	
    77	- AGENTS.md section order
    78	- docs tree templates
    79	- sample feature module with README + requirements separation
    80	- owning GOAL/README status rules
    81	- leaf-document link rules
    82	- validation checklist
    83	- per-project skill maintenance and contract migration
    84	
    85	## Demo Pack
    86	
    87	If the target repo needs a fast bootstrap, adapt the included demo harness from
    88	`assets/demo-harness/` and replace every placeholder with target-project facts.
    89	The demo pack includes:
    90	
    91	- a root `AGENTS.md` with documentation governance and execution-safety rules
    92	- a Cursor-native `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` gate (`alwaysApply: true`)
    93	- the `docs/` entry points
    94	- reference docs for architecture, interfaces, and validation
    95	- one sample feature module showing README + requirements separation
    96	
    97	Use it as a starting shape, not as a final domain model.
    98	
    99	## Suite Maintenance Boundary
   100	
   101	This repository is the canonical maintenance source for independent harness skills. It does not
   102	provide a bundle manifest, installer, automatic overwrite, or target-project upgrade command.
   103	Projects may maintain the full suite, a subset, or local extensions in grouped or flat paths.
   104	
   105	`add-idea` is the explicit docs-only intake for unclear or clear product/engineering ideas. It runs
   106	the Grill protocol when needed, chooses a new or existing Feature owner, and materializes
   107	requirements, Specs, and conditional ADRs before later implementation workflows.
   108	
   109	Recommended maintenance flow:
   110	
   111	1. Read the suite [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) and
   112	   [`UPGRADING.md`](../UPGRADING.md).
   113	2. Inspect the target project's actual skill registry, layout, local extensions, and working tree.
   114	3. Compare and update only the individual skills the target uses; do not normalize paths or replace
   115	   directories containing unclassified local content.
   116	4. When adopting the full lifecycle change, maintain shared contracts first, then producer and
   117	   consumer skills, then patch target-owned governance.
   118	5. Follow the suite [`AGENTS.md` patch contract](../README.md) to incrementally update existing target
   119	   rules; never replace target-owned rules or Feature docs.
   120	
   121	See `references/harness-bootstrap.md` for docs scaffolding and maintenance order. Target repository
   122	history, reviewed diffs, and validation evidence remain the truth for what that project maintains.

1	# Harness Bootstrap Reference
     2	
     3	## 1. Target shape
     4	
     5	The harness should expose four things:
     6	
     7	1. where to start reading;
     8	2. how the repo is organized;
     9	3. where expected behavior, current state, and durable progress are owned;
    10	4. how to verify a change.
    11	
    12	The implementation details of the product are not part of the harness.
    13	
    14	## 2. Root `AGENTS.md` skeleton
    15	
    16	Use this order:
    17	
    18	```md
    19	# Agent 开发规约
    20	
    21	> 项目上下文入口：[`docs/OVERVIEW.md`](docs/OVERVIEW.md)
    22	
    23	## 核心原则
    24	
    25	## 分层约束
    26	
    27	## 代码组织约束
    28	
    29	## 文档渐进式披露规则
    30	
    31	## 文档写入规则
    32	
    33	## 项目内置 skills
    34	
    35	## 强制执行流程门（Mandatory Execution Gate）
    36	
    37	## 防目标漂移（Anti-Drift）
    38	
    39	## Git Worktree 隔离开发
    40	
    41	## 测试规则
    42	
    43	## 历史教训
    44	```
    45	
    46	Keep the section names stable once published.
    47	
    48	The `强制执行流程门` section turns the harness from described guidance into an
    49	enforced workflow. It must require, in order:
    50	
    51	```text
    52	scope and ownership check
    53	  → freeze contracts, safety boundaries, and validation matrix
    54	  → update the owning GOAL/README current-state section
    55	  → implement within the declared boundary
    56	  → collect focused validation evidence
    57	  → update durable docs and append-only artifacts
    58	```
    59	
    60	The `防目标漂移` section keeps long runs aligned. The owning GOAL,
    61	`requirements.md`, and README current-state section are the durable anchors.
    62	Re-read them at the start of each work session, after context compaction, and
    63	before advancing through a validation gate.
    64	
    65	### Recommended current-state section
    66	
    67	```md
    68	## Current State
    69	
    70	- Status:
    71	- Completed:
    72	- Pending:
    73	- Blockers:
    74	- Next validation gate:
    75	- Evidence:
    76	```
    77	
    78	Use the session's planning surface for transient sequencing. Persist only
    79	durable state, decisions, blockers, and evidence in the owning documents.
    80	
    81	## 2.1 Repo-local skill registry
    82	
    83	If the repo uses project-local skills, add a concise registry in `AGENTS.md`.
    84	
    85	```md
    86	## Repo-local Skills
    87	
    88	- `.agents/skills/harness/add-idea`: unified docs-only idea intake; Grill when needed, then choose a new or existing Feature owner and materialize requirements, Specs, and conditional ADRs.
    89	- `.agents/skills/harness/document-organization-harness`: organize or repair project documentation, navigation, ownership, and governance.
    90	- `.agents/skills/harness/progressive-disclosure-docs`: enforce progressive disclosure, truth ownership, route overlays, and lifecycle structure.
    91	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-analysis`: investigate architecture, dataflow, route impact, and expected-vs-implemented gaps when shallow docs are insufficient.
    92	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-docs-workflow`: inspect docs impact before and after non-trivial code changes.
    93	- `.agents/skills/harness/external-collaboration-workflow`: preserve external proposal provenance and translate accepted items into internal contracts.
    94	- `.agents/skills/harness/refactor-large-modules`: split oversized or mixed-responsibility modules while preserving behavior and public contracts.
    95	```
    96	
    97	Do not force these exact skill names into every repo. The invariant is:
    98	
    99	- root instructions list available skills;
   100	- each skill has a clear trigger;
   101	- each skill owns one workflow;
   102	- detailed variants live inside the skill's `references/` or `assets/`.
   103	
   104	This source repository keeps canonical independent skills under `skills/harness/`. Target projects
   105	maintain only the skills they use, either grouped under `.agents/skills/harness/` or in an existing
   106	flat/custom registry. Do not move paths merely to match this repository.
   107	
   108	Recommended local skill shape:
   109	
   110	```text
   111	.agents/
   112	└── skills/
   113	    └── <skill-name>/
   114	        ├── SKILL.md
   115	        ├── agents/
   116	        │   └── openai.yaml
   117	        ├── references/
   118	        └── assets/
   119	```
   120	
   121	## 2.2 Maintain repo-local skills
   122	
   123	There is no suite installer or manifest. A target project maintains each selected skill through its
   124	normal reviewed change workflow. Read the source [`CHANGELOG.md`](../../CHANGELOG.md) and
   125	[`UPGRADING.md`](../../UPGRADING.md) before changing an existing copy.
   126	
   127	For each target:
   128	
   129	1. Read the actual skill registry and locate grouped, flat, partial, and project-specific skills.
   130	2. Record the target working state and isolate unrelated work according to target policy.
   131	3. Compare one canonical skill directory with its target counterpart.
   132	4. Classify canonical updates, local extensions, obsolete behavior, and uncertain content before
   133	   editing.
   134	5. Apply only reviewed changes; do not replace directories containing unclassified local files.
   135	6. Patch existing `AGENTS.md` and runtime-rule sections only after the corresponding target skill
   136	   paths exist.
   137	7. Validate frontmatter, provider metadata, links, docs routes, governance consistency, and the
   138	   target project's own checks.
   139	
   140	Projects adopting the full idea-to-implementation lifecycle maintain shared contracts and templates
   141	first, then `add-idea`, then consuming workflow skills, and finally target-owned governance. Projects
   142	may keep a smaller set; do not register or reference an absent skill.
   143	
   144	The demo remains a scaffolding example, not an installation payload. Copy or adapt demo files only
   145	when the target lacks an equivalent docs route, replace every demo fact, and preserve existing
   146	project safety, authorization, ownership, commands, and validation rules. Existing Features migrate
   147	to the Requirements/Spec/ADR model only when related work touches them.
   148	
   149	## 2.3 Cursor native execution gate (`.cursor/rules`)
   150	
   151	In a Cursor repo, land the execution gate in two always-visible places:
   152	
   153	1. `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` with `alwaysApply: true`;
   154	2. root `AGENTS.md` under `## 强制执行流程门（Mandatory Execution Gate）`.
   155	
   156	The gate enforces contract freeze, bounded implementation, focused validation,
   157	and durable documentation synchronization. It does not require delegation.
   158	Delegation remains opt-in and requires explicit user authorization.
   159	
   160	## 3. Docs tree skeleton
   161	
   162	```text
   163	docs/
   164	├── OVERVIEW.md
   165	├── feature/
   166	│   ├── INDEX.md
   167	│   └── <module>/
   168	│       ├── README.md
   169	│       ├── INDEX.md          # only when the module is large
   170	│       ├── requirements.md   # expected behavior and acceptance
   171	│       ├── specs/            # bounded implementation contracts; lazy
   172	│       ├── decisions/        # Feature-local ADRs; lazy
   173	│       ├── design.md         # stable shared design reference
   174	│       └── data-model.md     # stable table/contract reference
   175	├── reference/
   176	│   ├── INDEX.md
   177	│   ├── decisions/           # cross-Feature/system ADRs; lazy
   178	│   ├── architecture.md
   179	│   ├── interfaces.md
   180	│   └── runbook-testing.md
   181	├── collaboration/
   182	│   └── INDEX.md
   183	└── archive/
   184	    └── INDEX.md
   185	```
   186	
   187	The owning Feature README or GOAL records current implementation state,
   188	contract links, completed work, pending work, blockers, and the next validation
   189	gate. Requirements own expected behavior; Specs own bounded implementation
   190	contracts; ADRs own durable rationale. Do not create a parallel control plane.
   191	
   192	## 3.1 Feature granularity and autonomous governance
   193	
   194	Encode these rules in root `AGENTS.md`:
   195	
   196	```text
   197	一功能一目录：独立 feature（自有目标/里程碑、或自有契约/产出、或独立生命周期、
   198	  或 leaf ≥ 3 / 单文件 ≥ 500 行）必须独立成 docs/feature/<feature>/ 带自己的 README。
   199	自主维护：非 trivial 代码 / 契约变更后，同任务内主动更新 owning feature README、
   200	  requirements、feature/INDEX、OVERVIEW、反链及受影响的 interfaces/runbook。
   201	自主调整：发现大类下子主题膨胀时，主动提议拆成独立 feature。
   202	拆分不破链：父 INDEX/OVERVIEW 增路由、leaf 增反链、旧路径迁移而非并存。
   203	```
   204	
   205	## 4. Leaf-document rules
   206	
   207	Every leaf doc should begin with a parent link.
   208	
   209	```md
   210	> 上级：../README.md
   211	```
   212	
   213	For deeper locations, use a repo-root link:
   214	
   215	```md
   216	> 上级：[/docs/OVERVIEW.md](/docs/OVERVIEW.md)
   217	```
   218	
   219	Rules:
   220	
   221	- every leaf must be reachable from a parent index;
   222	- every leaf must point back up;
   223	- avoid orphan docs;
   224	- avoid deep `../` chains when a repo-root link is clearer.
   225	
   226	## 5. Durable status rule
   227	
   228	Use the owning GOAL/README when work has meaningful dependencies, staged
   229	validation, multiple owners, or a durable audit requirement.
   230	
   231	Update only these durable fields:
   232	
   233	1. expected behavior and acceptance;
   234	2. current implementation state;
   235	3. completed and pending work;
   236	4. blockers and decisions;
   237	5. next validation gate;
   238	6. stable evidence and append-only artifact locations.
   239	
   240	Transient session sequencing stays in the active planning surface and is not
   241	promoted into a separate repository control plane.
   242	
   243	## 6. Validation checklist
   244	
   245	- Start at `AGENTS.md`.
   246	- Reach `docs/OVERVIEW.md`.
   247	- Reach `docs/feature/INDEX.md` and `docs/reference/INDEX.md`.
   248	- Reach `docs/collaboration/INDEX.md` without treating external sources as internal contracts.
   249	- Reach at least one module README.
   250	- Walk back to the root through parent links.
   251	- Confirm no leaf doc is orphaned.
   252	- Confirm archive material is not mixed into active paths.
   253	- Confirm the owning GOAL/README exposes current state and the next gate.
   254	
   255	## 7. Demo harness pack
   256	
   257	This skill includes a copyable demo pack at `assets/demo-harness/`.
   258	
   259	Expected copy target:
   260	
   261	```text
   262	<target-repo>/
   263	├── AGENTS.md
   264	└── docs/
   265	```
   266	
   267	After copying:
   268	
   269	1. Replace generic names with the target repo's actual module names.
   270	2. Delete the demo module if the repo already has a real feature module.
   271	3. Keep `OVERVIEW.md`, `feature/INDEX.md`, `reference/INDEX.md`, and
   272	   `archive/INDEX.md`.
   273	4. Add repo-local skills to `AGENTS.md` only if they exist or will be installed.
   274	5. Run the validation checklist above.
     1	# Agent 开发规约
     2	
     3	> 项目上下文入口：[`docs/OVERVIEW.md`](docs/OVERVIEW.md)
     4	
     5	开始任何重要开发前，先读 `docs/OVERVIEW.md`。本仓库采用 docs-first、结构化契约、分层清晰、测试可执行的 harness 工作方式。禁止把密钥、凭证、私有运行时数据或敏感内容写入 docs、日志或用户可见输出。
     6	
     7	## 核心原则
     8	
     9	- **Docs-first**：新增模块、接口或执行方式前，先确认 owning feature 和参考文档。
    10	- **单一事实来源（SSOT）**：每条稳定规则只保留一个 owner。
    11	- **结构化契约**：API、配置、脚本、目录与测试命名使用明确约定。
    12	- **分层不反向**：控制层保持薄，编排放在服务层，底层不反向依赖上层。
    13	- **真实路径验证**：新增或修改能力必须留下可验证证据。
    14	
    15	## 分层约束
    16	
    17	按项目实际技术栈填写依赖方向、禁止跨层调用和外部系统边界。
    18	
    19	## 代码组织约束
    20	
    21	- 先找 owning module，再按 layer 放文件。
    22	- 新建前按 endpoint、schema、表名、配置键和 domain noun 搜索现有 owner。
    23	- 测试布局与被验证的代码层级保持对应。
    24	- 框架细则服从仓库既有约定。
    25	- 非 trivial 实施前冻结模块 owner、公共接口、依赖方向、可变状态 owner、文件预算和测试归属。
    26	- 新增或本轮修改的手写文件不得超过 1000 物理行；800 行触发职责拆分评审，不得机械切成 numbered part 文件。
    27	
    28	## 文档渐进式披露规则
    29	
    30	```text
    31	Level 0: AGENTS.md               → 项目开发规约与读取入口
    32	Level 1: docs/OVERVIEW.md        → 项目地图与活动模块
    33	Level 2F: docs/feature/INDEX.md  → 功能模块索引
    34	Level 2R: docs/reference/INDEX.md → 架构 / 接口 / 测试等稳定参考
    35	Level 2C: docs/collaboration/INDEX.md → 外部来源、版本绑定与内部采纳路由
    36	Level 2A: docs/archive/INDEX.md  → 历史归档，默认不读
    37	Level 3: docs/feature/<module>/  → 模块 README / INDEX
    38	Level 4: 具体设计 / RCA，仅按需读取
    39	```
    40	
    41	Agent 读取规则：`OVERVIEW.md -> feature/reference INDEX -> 按需读 1-3 个相关文档`。禁止全量读取 `docs/`。
    42	
    43	### 双向可追溯
    44	
    45	1. 从 `AGENTS.md` 沿 OVERVIEW、INDEX、子 INDEX 到 leaf 始终可达。
    46	2. 每个 leaf 顶部必须有上级链接。
    47	3. 跨多层目录的链接优先使用项目根路径。
    48	4. 移动文档时同时修复入口链接和反向链接。
    49	
    50	## 文档写入规则
    51	
    52	- 独立 feature 命中自有目标、契约、生命周期，或 leaf ≥ 3、单文件 ≥ 500 行时，建立 `docs/feature/<feature>/` 和 README。
    53	- `requirements.md` 记录 expected behavior 与 acceptance。
    54	- active frozen Spec 记录 bounded implementation contract；accepted ADR 记录 durable architecture rationale。
    55	- `README.md` / `INDEX.md` 只记录 current implementation、contract links、routing、completed、pending、blockers 和 next validation gate。
    56	- 非 trivial 代码、契约或运行方式变更后，同步 owning README、requirements、feature INDEX、OVERVIEW 及受影响的 reference docs。
    57	- 历史计划、旧结论和 RCA 放入 `docs/archive/` 并标记状态。
    58	- 任何新增 leaf 都要同时增加父级路由和上级链接。
    59	
    60	## 项目内置 skills
    61	
    62	- `.agents/skills/harness/add-idea`：统一接收新 idea；边界不清时逐题 Grill，确认后路由到新 Feature 或现有 Feature，并创建/patch requirements、Spec 与 conditional ADR；不实施代码。
    63	- `.agents/skills/harness/document-organization-harness`：组织文档结构、索引、模块边界与导航规则。
    64	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-analysis`：现有 docs 不足或链路复杂时进行架构、数据流、时序与风险分析。
    65	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-docs-workflow`：非 trivial 开发前后扫描 owning docs 并判断文档影响。
    66	- `.agents/skills/harness/progressive-disclosure-docs`：审计渐进式披露、SSOT、feature 粒度和双向可追溯。
    67	- `.agents/skills/harness/external-collaboration-workflow`：管理外部问题包、方案来源、采纳和内部合同转译。
    68	- `.agents/skills/harness/refactor-large-modules`：按稳定责任拆分大文件，保持公共契约和行为等价。
    69	
    70	## 强制执行流程门（Mandatory Execution Gate）
    71	
    72	非 trivial 的实现、修改、开发或修复任务，在写实现代码前依次完成：
    73	
    74	1. 未成形 idea 先使用 `add-idea` 完成边界确认与 Feature owner 路由；随后定位 owning module、requirements、active Spec、accepted ADR、README 和关键代码入口。
    75	2. contract-affecting implementation 必须引用 frozen Spec；冻结 schema、字段、状态、安全边界和验证矩阵。
    76	3. 在 owning GOAL/README 记录 completed、pending、blockers 和 next validation gate。
    77	4. 在声明边界内实施，保留不相关的现有修改。
    78	5. 运行聚焦验证，再运行与影响范围匹配的广泛检查。
    79	6. 将稳定状态、决策和证据同步到 owning docs 和 append-only artifacts。
    80	
    81	本门不自动授权委派。只有用户明确要求时才使用边界清晰的 owner scope；修改重叠时使用隔离 worktree。
    82	
    83	Cursor 环境下，本门同时由 `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` 每轮注入。
    84	
    85	## 防目标漂移（Anti-Drift）
    86	
    87	- owning GOAL、requirements 和 README current-state section 是执行锚点。
    88	- 每个工作 session 开始、上下文压缩后和推进验证门前重新读取这些文档。
    89	- 验证门通过后立即更新 durable state 与证据。
    90	- 每个非 trivial 动作前确认它直接推进目标且不跨越安全边界。
    91	
    92	## Git Worktree 隔离开发
    93	
    94	- 只有用户要求或并行修改会重叠时才创建 worktree。
    95	- worktree 使用明确的 owner scope，完成后由主 agent 集成和验证。
    96	- 不得为获得干净状态而丢弃无关修改。
    97	
    98	## 测试规则
    99	
   100	- 新增或修改功能必须更新对应测试。
   101	- 修改接口、运行方式或验证方式时同步参考文档。
   102	- 先运行聚焦测试，再运行影响范围支持的广泛检查。
   103	- 文档变更至少执行链接校验与格式检查。
   104	
   105	## 历史教训
   106	
   107	1. 模板不得保留废弃路径诱导新项目走错层级。
   108	2. 架构外部环节应在 OVERVIEW、reference 和 owning README 中可发现。
   109	3. docs 双向可追溯是硬约束。
   110	4. 稳定进度和证据必须回写到 owning docs，不能只存在于会话上下文。
     1	---
     2	description: Harness execution gate for contract freeze, bounded implementation, validation evidence, and durable documentation synchronization.
     3	alwaysApply: true
     4	---
     5	
     6	# 强制执行流程门（每轮生效）
     7	
     8	命中「实现 / 修改 / 开发 / 修复」类非 trivial 编码任务时，写实现代码前必须完成以下检查；单文件 trivial fix 可使用精简验证。
     9	
    10	## 必须按序执行
    11	
    12	1. **确认 owner 与范围**：未成形 idea 先进入 `add-idea`；随后定位 owning module、requirements、active Spec、accepted ADR、当前实现入口和禁止跨越的边界。
    13	2. **契约先行**：contract-affecting implementation 必须引用 frozen Spec；冻结 schema、字段、状态、安全边界和验证矩阵，blocking ADR 未 accepted 时停止。
    14	3. **更新 durable state**：在 owning GOAL/README 记录已完成、待完成、阻塞和下一验证门。
    15	4. **边界内实施**：只修改声明范围内的代码与文档；保留不相关的现有修改。
    16	5. **逐门验证**：先运行聚焦验证，再运行与影响范围匹配的广泛检查；未通过不得提升证据状态。
    17	6. **稳定收口**：将最终状态、决策和证据同步到 owning docs 与 append-only artifacts。
    18	
    19	## 委派边界
    20	
    21	本规则不自动授权委派。只有用户明确要求时，才使用边界清晰的 owner scope；修改范围重叠时使用隔离 worktree，主 agent 负责集成与验证。
    22	
    23	## 自检
    24	
    25	- [ ] owner、requirements、active Spec、blocking ADR 和安全边界是否明确？
    26	- [ ] owning GOAL/README 是否记录当前状态与下一验证门？
    27	- [ ] 当前动作是否直接推进目标且不越界？
    28	- [ ] 验证证据是否足以支持当前结论？
    29	- [ ] 稳定文档与索引是否同步？

     7	## 核心原则
     8	
     9	- **Docs-first**：新增模块、接口或执行方式前，先确认 owning feature 和参考文档。
    10	- **单一事实来源（SSOT）**：每条稳定规则只保留一个 owner。
    11	- **结构化契约**：API、配置、脚本、目录与测试命名使用明确约定。
    12	- **分层不反向**：控制层保持薄，编排放在服务层，底层不反向依赖上层。
    13	- **真实路径验证**：新增或修改能力必须留下可验证证据。
    14	
    15	## 分层约束
    16	
    17	按项目实际技术栈填写依赖方向、禁止跨层调用和外部系统边界。
    18	
    19	## 代码组织约束
    20	
    21	- 先找 owning module，再按 layer 放文件。
    22	- 新建前按 endpoint、schema、表名、配置键和 domain noun 搜索现有 owner。
    23	- 测试布局与被验证的代码层级保持对应。
    24	- 框架细则服从仓库既有约定。
    25	- 非 trivial 实施前冻结模块 owner、公共接口、依赖方向、可变状态 owner、文件预算和测试归属。
    26	- 新增或本轮修改的手写文件不得超过 1000 物理行；800 行触发职责拆分评审，不得机械切成 numbered part 文件。
    27	
    28	## 文档渐进式披露规则
    29	
    30	```text
    31	Level 0: AGENTS.md               → 项目开发规约与读取入口
    32	Level 1: docs/OVERVIEW.md        → 项目地图与活动模块
    33	Level 2F: docs/feature/INDEX.md  → 功能模块索引
    34	Level 2R: docs/reference/INDEX.md → 架构 / 接口 / 测试等稳定参考
    35	Level 2C: docs/collaboration/INDEX.md → 外部来源、版本绑定与内部采纳路由
    36	Level 2A: docs/archive/INDEX.md  → 历史归档，默认不读
    37	Level 3: docs/feature/<module>/  → 模块 README / INDEX
    38	Level 4: 具体设计 / RCA，仅按需读取
    39	```
    40	
    41	Agent 读取规则：`OVERVIEW.md -> feature/reference INDEX -> 按需读 1-3 个相关文档`。禁止全量读取 `docs/`。
    42	
    43	### 双向可追溯
    44	
    45	1. 从 `AGENTS.md` 沿 OVERVIEW、INDEX、子 INDEX 到 leaf 始终可达。
    46	2. 每个 leaf 顶部必须有上级链接。
    47	3. 跨多层目录的链接优先使用项目根路径。
    48	4. 移动文档时同时修复入口链接和反向链接。
    49	
    50	## 文档写入规则
    51	
    52	- 独立 feature 命中自有目标、契约、生命周期，或 leaf ≥ 3、单文件 ≥ 500 行时，建立 `docs/feature/<feature>/` 和 README。
    53	- `requirements.md` 记录 expected behavior 与 acceptance。
    54	- active frozen Spec 记录 bounded implementation contract；accepted ADR 记录 durable architecture rationale。
    55	- `README.md` / `INDEX.md` 只记录 current implementation、contract links、routing、completed、pending、blockers 和 next validation gate。
    56	- 非 trivial 代码、契约或运行方式变更后，同步 owning README、requirements、feature INDEX、OVERVIEW 及受影响的 reference docs。
    57	- 历史计划、旧结论和 RCA 放入 `docs/archive/` 并标记状态。
    58	- 任何新增 leaf 都要同时增加父级路由和上级链接。
    59	
    60	## 项目内置 skills
    61	
    62	- `.agents/skills/harness/add-idea`：统一接收新 idea；边界不清时逐题 Grill，确认后路由到新 Feature 或现有 Feature，并创建/patch requirements、Spec 与 conditional ADR；不实施代码。
    63	- `.agents/skills/harness/document-organization-harness`：组织文档结构、索引、模块边界与导航规则。
    64	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-analysis`：现有 docs 不足或链路复杂时进行架构、数据流、时序与风险分析。
    65	- `.agents/skills/harness/project-docs-workflow`：非 trivial 开发前后扫描 owning docs 并判断文档影响。
    66	- `.agents/skills/harness/progressive-disclosure-docs`：审计渐进式披露、SSOT、feature 粒度和双向可追溯。
    67	- `.agents/skills/harness/external-collaboration-workflow`：管理外部问题包、方案来源、采纳和内部合同转译。
    68	- `.agents/skills/harness/refactor-large-modules`：按稳定责任拆分大文件，保持公共契约和行为等价。
    69	
    70	## 强制执行流程门（Mandatory Execution Gate）
    71	
    72	非 trivial 的实现、修改、开发或修复任务，在写实现代码前依次完成：
    73	
    74	1. 未成形 idea 先使用 `add-idea` 完成边界确认与 Feature owner 路由；随后定位 owning module、requirements、active Spec、accepted ADR、README 和关键代码入口。
    75	2. contract-affecting implementation 必须引用 frozen Spec；冻结 schema、字段、状态、安全边界和验证矩阵。
    76	3. 在 owning GOAL/README 记录 completed、pending、blockers 和 next validation gate。
    77	4. 在声明边界内实施，保留不相关的现有修改。
    78	5. 运行聚焦验证，再运行与影响范围匹配的广泛检查。
    79	6. 将稳定状态、决策和证据同步到 owning docs 和 append-only artifacts。
    80	
    81	本门不自动授权委派。只有用户明确要求时才使用边界清晰的 owner scope；修改重叠时使用隔离 worktree。
    82	
    83	Cursor 环境下，本门同时由 `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` 每轮注入。
    84	
    85	## 防目标漂移（Anti-Drift）
    86	
    87	- owning GOAL、requirements 和 README current-state section 是执行锚点。
    88	- 每个工作 session 开始、上下文压缩后和推进验证门前重新读取这些文档。
    89	- 验证门通过后立即更新 durable state 与证据。
    90	- 每个非 trivial 动作前确认它直接推进目标且不跨越安全边界。
    91	
    92	## Git Worktree 隔离开发
    93	
    94	- 只有用户要求或并行修改会重叠时才创建 worktree。
    95	- worktree 使用明确的 owner scope，完成后由主 agent 集成和验证。
    96	- 不得为获得干净状态而丢弃无关修改。
    97	
    98	## 测试规则
    99	
   100	- 新增或修改功能必须更新对应测试。
   101	- 修改接口、运行方式或验证方式时同步参考文档。
   102	- 先运行聚焦测试，再运行影响范围支持的广泛检查。
   103	- 文档变更至少执行链接校验与格式检查。
   104	
   105	## 历史教训
   106	
   107	1. 模板不得保留废弃路径诱导新项目走错层级。
   108	2. 架构外部环节应在 OVERVIEW、reference 和 owning README 中可发现。
   109	3. docs 双向可追溯是硬约束。
   110	4. 稳定进度和证据必须回写到 owning docs，不能只存在于会话上下文。
     1	---
     2	description: Harness execution gate for contract freeze, bounded implementation, validation evidence, and durable documentation synchronization.
     3	alwaysApply: true
     4	---
     5	
     6	# 强制执行流程门（每轮生效）
     7	
     8	命中「实现 / 修改 / 开发 / 修复」类非 trivial 编码任务时，写实现代码前必须完成以下检查；单文件 trivial fix 可使用精简验证。
     9	
    10	## 必须按序执行
    11	
    12	1. **确认 owner 与范围**：未成形 idea 先进入 `add-idea`；随后定位 owning module、requirements、active Spec、accepted ADR、当前实现入口和禁止跨越的边界。
    13	2. **契约先行**：contract-affecting implementation 必须引用 frozen Spec；冻结 schema、字段、状态、安全边界和验证矩阵，blocking ADR 未 accepted 时停止。
    14	3. **更新 durable state**：在 owning GOAL/README 记录已完成、待完成、阻塞和下一验证门。
    15	4. **边界内实施**：只修改声明范围内的代码与文档；保留不相关的现有修改。
    16	5. **逐门验证**：先运行聚焦验证，再运行与影响范围匹配的广泛检查；未通过不得提升证据状态。
    17	6. **稳定收口**：将最终状态、决策和证据同步到 owning docs 与 append-only artifacts。
    18	
    19	## 委派边界
    20	
    21	本规则不自动授权委派。只有用户明确要求时，才使用边界清晰的 owner scope；修改范围重叠时使用隔离 worktree，主 agent 负责集成与验证。
    22	
    23	## 自检
    24	
    25	- [ ] owner、requirements、active Spec、blocking ADR 和安全边界是否明确？
    26	- [ ] owning GOAL/README 是否记录当前状态与下一验证门？
    27	- [ ] 当前动作是否直接推进目标且不越界？
    28	- [ ] 验证证据是否足以支持当前结论？
    29	- [ ] 稳定文档与索引是否同步？

FILE skills/harness/add-idea/SKILL.md
     1	---
     2	name: add-idea
     3	description: >-
     4	  Unified, docs-only entry for adding a product or engineering idea to a
     5	  harness-managed repository. Use when the user invokes add-idea or asks to
     6	  turn an idea into a new Feature or a bounded change to an existing Feature.
     7	  Inspect current owners first, Grill unclear ideas one decision at a time,
     8	  then create or patch requirements, a Spec, and conditional ADRs without
     9	  implementing code or publishing external issues.
    10	disable-model-invocation: true
    11	---
    12	
    13	# Add Idea
    14	
    15	Use this as the single explicit intake for an idea. The outcome is a clear,
    16	routed internal contract, not code implementation.
    17	
    18	Read [references/routing-contract.md](references/routing-contract.md) completely
    19	before deciding the route. When writing durable artifacts, also read
    20	`../progressive-disclosure-docs/references/feature-spec-decision-contract.md`.
    21	
    22	## Invariants
    23	
    24	- Keep the original user outcome visible while refining details.
    25	- Investigate repository facts; ask the user only for decisions.
    26	- Ask one question at a time during Grill and include a recommended answer with
    27	  a short rationale.
    28	- Do not write Feature, requirements, Spec, or ADR docs until the user confirms
    29	  the final shared-understanding summary.
    30	- The agent chooses the owner route from evidence. Ask the user only when two or
    31	  more owners remain equally valid or the choice changes a product boundary.
    32	- This skill never grants code implementation, deployment, training, execution,
    33	  external publication, or issue-tracker actions.
    34	- Do not persist interview transcripts or a separate idea backlog. Confirmed
    35	  content must return to the existing Feature/requirements/Spec/ADR owners.
    36	
    37	## Workflow
    38	
    39	### 1. Discover the current ownership map
    40	
    41	Read progressively:
    42	
    43	1. root `AGENTS.md` or equivalent;
    44	2. `docs/OVERVIEW.md`;
    45	3. `docs/feature/INDEX.md`;
    46	4. at most the likely owning Feature README/INDEX and `requirements.md` files;
    47	5. targeted reference docs and code only when they can settle a fact.
    48	
    49	Record in the session:
    50	
    51	- the problem, actor, and intended outcome;
    52	- candidate Feature owners and supporting evidence;
    53	- existing expected behavior and current implementation;
    54	- safety, authorization, public-contract, and data boundaries;
    55	- facts already established and decisions still open.
    56	
    57	Do not create a new Feature merely because the user used a new phrase. Prefer an
    58	existing owner when its responsibility and lifecycle genuinely cover the idea.
    59	
    60	### 2. Apply the clarity gate
    61	
    62	An idea is ready for routing only when these are clear enough to distinguish
    63	ownership and acceptance:
    64	
    65	- problem and intended user/business outcome;
    66	- in-scope and out-of-scope behavior;
    67	- measurable acceptance or an observable completion condition;
    68	- relevant constraints, safety, authorization, and compatibility boundaries;
    69	- candidate owner and affected contracts;
    70	- unresolved decisions that would change the owner, public behavior, schema,
    71	  state ownership, migration, validation, or rollback.
    72	
    73	If route-affecting ambiguity remains, enter Grill. If all items are already
    74	clear from the request and repository, skip Grill and summarize the inferred
    75	boundary for confirmation.
    76	
    77	### 3. Grill unclear ideas
    78	
    79	Walk the unresolved decision tree in dependency order:
    80	
    81	1. Ask exactly one decision question.
    82	2. Give the recommended answer and why it best fits current evidence.
    83	3. Wait for the user's answer before advancing.
    84	4. Update the in-session decision ledger: confirmed facts, user decisions,
    85	   rejected alternatives, open questions, and affected owners.
    86	5. Look up newly discoverable facts instead of asking for them.
    87	
    88	Do not draft contracts while questions remain open. When all blocking branches
    89	are resolved, present one compact shared-understanding summary containing:
    90	
    91	- problem and outcome;
    92	- scope and non-goals;
    93	- acceptance and stop conditions;
    94	- selected owner and affected contracts;
    95	- durable decisions and remaining non-blocking unknowns;
    96	- recommended documentation route.
    97	
    98	Ask for explicit confirmation. Continue only after the user confirms the
    99	summary or corrects it.
   100	
   101	### 4. Choose two independent routes
   102	
   103	Choose one **owner route**:
   104	
   105	- `CREATE_FEATURE`: the idea needs an independent durable owner.
   106	- `PATCH_FEATURE`: exactly one existing Feature owns the behavior.
   107	- `BLOCKED_OWNER`: ownership remains ambiguous or conflicts with project
   108	  boundaries; stop and surface the competing owners.
   109	
   110	Then choose one or more **artifact routes**:
   111	
   112	- `REQUIREMENTS_PATCH`: expected behavior, acceptance, non-goals, constraints,
   113	  or stop rules change.
   114	- `NEW_SPEC`: implementation-relevant contracts change, including public API,
   115	  schema, state machine, module ownership, data flow, migration, compatibility,
   116	  security, validation, rollout, or rollback.
   117	- `ADR_CANDIDATE`: a durable architecture decision meets the decision trigger.
   118	- `STATE_ONLY`: only the Feature's durable current-state summary or routing
   119	  changes; do not invent requirements or a Spec.
   120	- `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE`: the idea is a reversible local detail with no expected
   121	  behavior, contract, decision, or durable state impact; report the owner and
   122	  stop without changing docs.
   123	
   124	`CREATE_FEATURE` and `NEW_SPEC` are not opposites. A new Feature normally starts
   125	with requirements and may also receive its first Spec. An existing Feature may
   126	receive a requirements patch, a new Spec, an ADR, or a combination.
   127	
   128	State the chosen routes and evidence before writing. Do not ask the user to pick
   129	between routes when the repository evidence is decisive.
   130	
   131	### 5. Materialize the confirmed contract
   132	
   133	Follow the shared Feature/Spec/ADR contract.
   134	
   135	For `CREATE_FEATURE`:
   136	
   137	- create the Feature from
   138	  `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/feature-template/`;
   139	- replace every placeholder with confirmed content;
   140	- after faithfully materializing the confirmed boundary, set requirements to
   141	  `CONFIRMED`, record the real confirmation date/authority when known, and
   142	  update README requirements/route status; do not leave initial `DRAFT`
   143	  scaffolding or a stale contract-freeze blocker;
   144	- register it in `docs/feature/INDEX.md` and `docs/OVERVIEW.md`;
   145	- keep Feature lifecycle separate from Spec delivery status.
   146	
   147	For `PATCH_FEATURE`:
   148	
   149	- update the existing owner in place;
   150	- set a changed requirements revision to `CONFIRMED` only when the confirmed
   151	  shared-understanding summary fully covers that revision; otherwise stop
   152	  rather than writing a partial contract;
   153	- preserve unrelated requirements and current-state content;
   154	- add a new Spec instead of overwriting a validated or superseded Spec;
   155	- update parent routes and back-links only when new artifacts are created.
   156	
   157	For artifact routes:
   158	
   159	- when `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE` applies, write no docs and explain why;
   160	- write expected behavior only to `requirements.md`;
   161	- create a Spec and lazy index from `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/spec-template.md` and `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/spec-index-template.md` when `NEW_SPEC` applies;
   162	- create an ADR and lazy index from `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/adr-template.md` and `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/decision-index-template.md` only when the ADR trigger applies;
   163	- keep ADR-worthy rationale out of README and keep implementation design out of
   164	  requirements;
   165	- update README with links and compact status only;
   166	- append the durable transition to `changelog.md`.
   167	
   168	A blocking ADR stays `proposed` until the decision authority accepts it. A Spec
   169	cannot become `frozen` while blocking decisions or contract questions remain.
   170	
   171	### 6. Stop at the documentation gate
   172	
   173	Finish with:
   174	
   175	- selected owner route and rationale;
   176	- artifact routes and files created or updated;
   177	- requirements, Spec, and decision statuses;
   178	- unresolved blockers;
   179	- next documentation or validation gate;
   180	- explicit statement that implementation remains unauthorized.
   181	
   182	Do not implement code in the same invocation. A later implementation request
   183	must enter `project-docs-workflow` and re-check the frozen contracts.
   184	
   185	## Stop conditions
   186	
   187	Stop without expanding the change when:
   188	
   189	- the user has not confirmed shared understanding;
   190	- no owner can be selected without changing a product boundary;
   191	- expected behavior conflicts with an existing frozen contract;
   192	- a blocking architecture decision is still unresolved;
   193	- the requested artifact would create a second SSOT;
   194	- the request crosses a safety, authorization, data, or external-publication
   195	  boundary that the user has not explicitly approved.

     1	# Add Idea Routing Contract
     2	
     3	Use this contract to decide whether an idea creates a Feature or extends an
     4	existing Feature. Make the decision from repository evidence after the idea is
     5	clear; do not route from keywords alone.
     6	
     7	## 1. Session-only intake schema
     8	
     9	Keep this ledger in the conversation until shared understanding is confirmed:
    10	
    11	```text
    12	Problem:
    13	Actor / beneficiary:
    14	Desired outcome:
    15	In scope:
    16	Out of scope:
    17	Acceptance / observable completion:
    18	Constraints and safety boundaries:
    19	Candidate owners:
    20	Confirmed facts:
    21	User decisions:
    22	Rejected alternatives:
    23	Open questions:
    24	Affected contracts:
    25	```
    26	
    27	This ledger is not repository SSOT and must not be saved as `idea.md`,
    28	`interview.md`, or any parallel progress/control file.
    29	
    30	## 2. Clarity classification
    31	
    32	Classify the intake as:
    33	
    34	- `CLEAR`: ownership and acceptance can be decided from the request and current
    35	  repository evidence.
    36	- `GRILL_REQUIRED`: at least one unresolved decision can change ownership,
    37	  scope, public behavior, schema/state, safety, validation, or rollback.
    38	- `BLOCKED_FACT`: a required fact should be discoverable but cannot currently be
    39	  verified. Report the missing source instead of asking the user to guess.
    40	
    41	Do not Grill optional implementation details that can remain open in a draft
    42	Spec. Grill only decisions needed to define the boundary or freeze a contract.
    43	
    44	## 3. Owner route
    45	
    46	### `PATCH_FEATURE`
    47	
    48	Choose an existing Feature when all are true:
    49	
    50	1. one current Feature already owns the affected user/business behavior;
    51	2. the idea extends or corrects that responsibility without introducing an
    52	   independent long-term outcome;
    53	3. acceptance can be expressed as an addition or revision to that Feature's
    54	   requirements;
    55	4. lifecycle, authorization, evidence, and release boundaries remain owned by
    56	   the same Feature;
    57	5. no new top-level public artifact or cross-Feature coordination owner is
    58	   required.
    59	
    60	Evidence should include the owning README/requirements route and, when relevant,
    61	current code or interface references.
    62	
    63	### `CREATE_FEATURE`
    64	
    65	Create a Feature when any strong ownership signal applies:
    66	
    67	- independent user or business outcome;
    68	- independently accepted, deprecated, or maintained lifecycle;
    69	- independent public contract, data product, persistent artifact, or external
    70	  integration boundary;
    71	- distinct safety, authorization, evidence, or rollout boundary;
    72	- cross-Feature change that needs one durable coordination owner;
    73	- its own roadmap or multiple delivery Specs;
    74	- existing owner would become a catch-all with unrelated responsibilities;
    75	- existing granularity rules already require promotion to a Feature.
    76	
    77	Do not use document count alone when the content still belongs to one owner.
    78	Document growth is supporting evidence, not a substitute for responsibility.
    79	
    80	### `BLOCKED_OWNER`
    81	
    82	Stop when:
    83	
    84	- two Features both plausibly own the behavior and the difference affects public
    85	  contracts or lifecycle;
    86	- the proposed owner contradicts existing requirements or architecture rules;
    87	- the idea is actually a project-wide policy and no system-level owner exists;
    88	- selecting an owner would silently redefine an existing Feature boundary.
    89	
    90	Present the competing owners, consequences, and recommendation as one decision
    91	question.
    92	
    93	## 4. Artifact route
    94	
    95	Owner routing and artifact routing are independent.
    96	
    97	| Change | Required artifact |
    98	|---|---|
    99	| Expected behavior, acceptance, non-goals, NFR, stop rule | `REQUIREMENTS_PATCH` |
   100	| API/schema/state/dataflow/module/migration/test/rollout contract | `NEW_SPEC` |
   101	| Durable architecture choice with real alternatives | `ADR_CANDIDATE` |
   102	| Current snapshot or route only | `STATE_ONLY` |
   103	| Reversible local detail with no durable truth change | `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE` |
   104	
   105	A single idea may produce `REQUIREMENTS_PATCH + NEW_SPEC + ADR_CANDIDATE`.
   106	
   107	### When a Spec is not required
   108	
   109	Do not force a Spec for:
   110	
   111	- wording-only requirements clarification with no implementation consequence;
   112	- current-state correction that does not change expected behavior;
   113	- trivial local implementation detail already governed by a frozen or validated Spec;
   114	- reversible local detail with no expected behavior, contract, decision, or durable state impact (`NO_DURABLE_CHANGE`);
   115	- archive or route repair with no contract change.
   116	
   117	### When a Spec is required
   118	
   119	Create a Spec when implementation must freeze any of:
   120	
   121	- public interface or schema;
   122	- data ownership, mutable state, lifecycle, or state transition;
   123	- cross-module dependency or integration behavior;
   124	- migration, compatibility, rollout, rollback, or stop behavior;
   125	- security, privacy, authorization, or evidence boundary;
   126	- module ownership, file/interface boundary, or test seam;
   127	- validation matrix and pass criteria for a non-trivial change.
   128	
   129	## 5. ADR trigger
   130	
   131	Create an ADR only when the decision is durable and all three default signals
   132	are present:
   133	
   134	1. changing it later has meaningful cost;
   135	2. a future maintainer could reasonably choose differently without the context;
   136	3. credible alternatives exist and the choice reflects a real trade-off.
   137	
   138	Public data ownership, security boundary, persistence technology, deployment
   139	topology, cross-Feature integration, or irreversible migration decisions should
   140	be treated as strong ADR candidates.
   141	
   142	Do not create an ADR for reversible local implementation details, obvious
   143	conformance to an existing contract, formatting, naming with no domain effect,
   144	or choices already owned by an accepted ADR.
   145	
   146	## 6. Decision output
   147	
   148	Before writing files, report:
   149	
   150	```text
   151	Clarity: CLEAR | GRILL_COMPLETED
   152	Owner route: CREATE_FEATURE | PATCH_FEATURE | BLOCKED_OWNER
   153	Selected owner: <path or proposed feature slug>
   154	Owner evidence: <concise evidence>
   155	Artifact routes: [REQUIREMENTS_PATCH, NEW_SPEC, ADR_CANDIDATE, STATE_ONLY, NO_DURABLE_CHANGE]
   156	Blocking decisions: <none or list>
   157	Documentation authorization: docs-only
   158	Implementation authorization: none
   159	```
   160	
   161	The user confirms the shared boundary, not a menu of arbitrary route choices.

     1	# Feature, Spec, and Decision Contract
     2	
     3	Use this contract whenever a harness-managed repository creates or changes a
     4	Feature, implementation Spec, or architecture decision.
     5	
     6	## 1. Separate durable owners
     7	
     8	| Truth | Owner | Must not contain |
     9	|---|---|---|
    10	| Feature map and current capability/state | Feature `README.md` | detailed implementation design or decision rationale |
    11	| Expected behavior and acceptance | `requirements.md` | module layout, pseudocode, current implementation claims |
    12	| Bounded implementation contract | active `Spec` | product rationale duplicated from requirements |
    13	| Durable architecture rationale | `ADR` | progress tracking or full implementation plan |
    14	| Current implementation | code | claims about unimplemented future behavior |
    15	| State-transition history | `changelog.md` | mutable current snapshot |
    16	| Validation evidence | immutable artifact, ledger, or gate report | unsupported narrative claims |
    17	
    18	README links these owners and reports compact statuses; it does not duplicate
    19	their bodies.
    20	
    21	## 2. Default paths
    22	
    23	```text
    24	docs/feature/<feature>/
    25	├── INDEX.md                 # optional for large Features
    26	├── README.md                # Feature map and current state
    27	├── requirements.md          # expected behavior and acceptance
    28	├── specs/                   # create lazily
    29	│   ├── INDEX.md
    30	│   └── SPEC-YYYY-NNN-slug.md
    31	├── decisions/               # create lazily for Feature-local decisions
    32	│   ├── INDEX.md
    33	│   └── ADR-YYYY-NNN-slug.md
    34	└── changelog.md
    35	
    36	docs/reference/decisions/    # create lazily for cross-Feature/system decisions
    37	├── INDEX.md
    38	└── ADR-YYYY-NNN-slug.md
    39	```
    40	
    41	Create lazy indexes from `assets/spec-index-template.md` and
    42	`assets/decision-index-template.md`. Preserve an existing repository ADR
    43	convention when it already has one clear owner. Never create a second ADR tree.
    44	Every Spec/ADR must be reachable from its Feature or reference index and link
    45	back to that owner.
    46	
    47	IDs are immutable. Use the next available year-local sequence in the owning
    48	index unless the repository already defines another scheme.
    49	
    50	## 3. Independent lifecycles
    51	
    52	### Feature lifecycle
    53	
    54	```text
    55	PROPOSED -> ACTIVE -> MAINTENANCE -> DEPRECATED -> RETIRED
    56	     \-> ABANDONED
    57	```
    58	
    59	A Feature is a durable capability owner. Its lifecycle does not move to
    60	`IMPLEMENTATION_ACTIVE` every time a new change is built.
    61	
    62	### Requirements status
    63	
    64	```text
    65	DRAFT -> CONFIRMED -> SUPERSEDED
    66	```
    67	
    68	Changing confirmed expected behavior requires a new revision entry and reopens
    69	any affected frozen Spec.
    70	
    71	### Spec lifecycle
    72	
    73	```text
    74	DRAFT -> FROZEN -> IMPLEMENTATION_ACTIVE -> VALIDATION_ACTIVE
    75	      -> VALIDATED | REJECTED | SUPERSEDED
    76	```
    77	
    78	A Spec is `FROZEN` only when its required contracts and decisions are resolved.
    79	Changing a frozen public contract returns it to `DRAFT` or creates a superseding
    80	Spec; record the transition in the Feature changelog.
    81	
    82	### ADR lifecycle
    83	
    84	```text
    85	PROPOSED -> ACCEPTED | REJECTED
    86	ACCEPTED -> SUPERSEDED | DEPRECATED
    87	```
    88	
    89	Do not rewrite an accepted ADR to express a new decision. Create a new ADR and
    90	link `supersedes` / `superseded_by` in both records.
    91	
    92	## 4. Feature creation gate
    93	
    94	A new Feature requires:
    95	
    96	- an independent durable owner under the Feature granularity rules;
    97	- problem, actor/outcome, scope, and non-goals;
    98	- expected behavior and measurable/observable acceptance;
    99	- constraints, NFRs, safety/authorization, and stop rules;
   100	- a README current-state route and changelog;
   101	- registration in `docs/feature/INDEX.md` and `docs/OVERVIEW.md`.
   102	
   103	Creating a Feature does not automatically require an ADR. Create the first Spec
   104	only when implementation-relevant contracts are known or need to be frozen.
   105	
   106	## 5. Spec freeze gate
   107	
   108	A Spec may become `FROZEN` only when applicable fields are complete:
   109	
   110	- requirements version/reference;
   111	- scope and non-goals;
   112	- accepted blocking ADR references;
   113	- public API, schema, artifact, and compatibility contracts;
   114	- data flow, state machine, mutable-state owner, and serialization boundaries;
   115	- module responsibilities, interfaces, dependency direction, and reuse boundary;
   116	- security, privacy, authorization, and evidence boundaries;
   117	- migration and backward-compatibility behavior;
   118	- validation matrix with seams, tests, evidence, and pass criteria;
   119	- rollout, rollback, stop conditions, and failure handling;
   120	- zero blocking open questions;
   121	- explicit docs-only versus implementation authorization.
   122	
   123	Not every Spec needs every section. Mark a section `Not applicable` with a
   124	reason rather than silently omitting a risk-bearing category.
   125	
   126	A frozen Spec is `IMPLEMENTATION_READY` only when code entry points, file
   127	budgets, test owners, next gate, and separate implementation authorization are
   128	also clear.
   129	
   130	## 6. ADR trigger and gate
   131	
   132	Create an ADR when a decision is difficult to reverse, surprising without its
   133	context, and based on a real trade-off. Strong candidates include system/Feature
   134	boundaries, data ownership, persistent storage, public protocol, deployment
   135	topology, security model, and irreversible migration.
   136	
   137	A blocking ADR must be `ACCEPTED` before a dependent Spec becomes `FROZEN`.
   138	`PROPOSED` ADRs contain a recommendation, not an accepted decision. `REJECTED`
   139	ADRs remain discoverable so the same option is not repeatedly reconsidered.
   140	
   141	## 7. Patch rules
   142	
   143	For an existing Feature:
   144	
   145	- patch `requirements.md` only when expected behavior changes;
   146	- create a new Spec for a new bounded implementation change;
   147	- do not overwrite a validated or superseded Spec;
   148	- create an ADR only for ADR-worthy choices, not every design detail;
   149	- keep current implementation claims in README aligned with code;
   150	- append state transitions to `changelog.md`;
   151	- route completed historical Specs according to the repository archive policy.
   152	
   153	## 8. Progressive disclosure
   154	
   155	Default reading remains:
   156	
   157	```text
   158	AGENTS -> OVERVIEW -> Feature INDEX -> Feature README/requirements
   159	```
   160	
   161	Read an active Spec only for implementation, review, validation, or contract
   162	questions. Read an ADR only when its scope affects the current decision. Do not
   163	load every historical Spec or ADR.
   164	
   165	## 9. Confirmation and authorization
   166	
   167	A user confirmation freezes the described product/engineering boundary; it does
   168	not grant implementation, deployment, execution, publication, or destructive
   169	actions. When `add-idea` faithfully materializes the confirmed boundary, change
   170	the affected requirements revision from `DRAFT` to `CONFIRMED` and update the
   171	Feature README route/status in the same write. Store decision authority and date
   172	only when the project can name them accurately. Never invent an approver identity.
